title: Kramer/Fauci by Daniel Fish at NYU Skirball #kramerfauci #danielfish ...
transcript: I love documentary theatre and I love the work I've seen by Daniel Fish — so this was a delight. In ‘93, Larry Kramer and Anthony Fauci did an hour-long segment on C-SPAN where they discussed the status of the AIDS epidemic at the time. This world premiere production superimposes their conversation word for word onto a stage that's completely bare, less a couple of absurd and unexpected design flourishes. Perhaps stripping it of any visual context is what makes it feel as urgent and scorching as ever. It's also certainly the fantastic performances from Thomas Jay Ryan and Will Brill. Consistent with the work I've seen by Daniel Fish, the deconstructed nature of this piece makes it feel very intimate. Conversely though, there's a vastness conveyed by how big the stage is, as if to imply that even the most urgent messages often fall upon deaf ears, never reaching beyond the void. I think this piece speaks to a feeling that lots of people have, that there's an almost insurmountable cloud of complacency and bureaucracy from those who should be leading, wrapping us in a twilight zone of pretending that everything's fine when we know it's not. This play is just an hour long, but it's clearly packed. Kramer/Fauci is running at Skirball only through next weekend. With that, another program for my collection.
